messages:
harper: Running into a weird client-side stall in the js/browser SDK when using the paginator in offline->reconnect scenarios. It seems to stop fetching new pages after a burst of 401s from our auth proxy.

mina: Is this the latest browser-sdk@1.7? Any stack or logs?

harper: Yep 1.7. Logs show the paginator holds the in-flight window while triggering token refreshes. After reconnecting the auth proxy returns 200 for the refresh but the paginator never resumes. Snippet:
```
DEBUG paginator acquire-window 6
DEBUG transport -> /v1/complete (id=72) -> 401
DEBUG auth startRefresh singleflight: miss
DEBUG auth refresh done tok_zzz
DEBUG paginator waiting-on-window (id=72)
// no further requests
```

zack: That pattern smells like refresh being awaited while the window lock is held. Browser event loop differences could make this surface only in the browser SDK. Node doesn't hit it because we queue refresh differently.

lee: Possible fixes: 1) always release window lock before awaiting refresh, 2) background single-flight refresh, or 3) make paginator tolerant to long-held locks by exposing a timeout and diagnostic hook. I prefer #2+3: single-flight to avoid duplicate refreshes and a diagnostic hook so customers can opt into telemetry if they hit stalls.

harper: I prototyped 2: run refresh in background and let inflight request mark itself as waiting. That removed the stall in my tests. I'll open a tiny repro and a test that simulates reconnect bursts.

ci-bot: CI started for branch harper/browser-paginator-auth-repro #3

mina: Please include a short note in release notes about potential hangs for browser-sdk@1.7 and mitigation steps (pin to 1.6 or apply patch). Also add an example in docs showing using paginator.setOptions({windowMonitorMs:5000}) to surface long holds.

zack: Also update SDK parity doc: browser should match node/python single-flight semantics. We'll add a unit test across SDKs to assert only one refresh runs when N callers see 401s.

harper: PR coming shortly. Will tag you both. Thanks.
